original_question: In the two-server queue case m = 2 with stationary waiting time D, when the load satisfies rho in (1, 2) and the service-time distribution is heavy-tailed but has all power moments finite, for example P(sigma_1 > x) = exp(-x^beta) for some beta in (0, 1), what is the asymptotic behavior of P(D > x) as x becomes large?
target_in_paper: The draft is trying to capture the unresolved two-server GI/GI/2 FCFS tail-asymptotics problem in the regime 1<ρ<2: determine the exact large-x behavior of the stationary waiting-time tail P(D>x) when the service-time law is heavy-tailed but lies outside the intermediate-regularly-varying case, with Weibull-type tails as the motivating example. arXiv:0909.0462 is explicitly a short open-problems note; the nearest precise formulation of this same gap is the 1<ρ<2 two-server statement restated as Theorem 1.2, together with the later Weibull-type remark that the known lower and upper bounds are not of the same order. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/0909.0462))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly singles out the two-server case m=2, the stationary waiting time D, the load window ρ∈(1,2), the heavy-tail setting, the focus on the asymptotic tail P(D>x) as x→∞, and the Weibull-type example with all power moments finite. Those are the right features of the paper’s unresolved gap beyond the solved intermediate-regular-variation case. ([lancaster.ac.uk](https://www.lancaster.ac.uk/staff/korshuno/publications/gi-gi-s.pdf))
missing_details: The queue should be identified as a stable GI/GI/2 first-come, first-served queue, not just a generic two-server queue.
The interarrival and service sequences should be named and normalized: i.i.d. interarrival times τ_n with mean a, i.i.d. service times σ_n with mean b, and load ρ=b/a.
The service-tail notation should be made explicit: B̄(x)=P{σ>x}.
The residual-service tail notation should be made explicit, because the known results are formulated in terms of it: B̄_r(x)=b^{-1}∫_x^∞ B̄(y)dy.
The draft should distinguish the assumptions on B from the assumptions on B_r.
The official paper-faithful framing is an open problem / unresolved case, not a theorem with a known answer.
The exact solved special case should be separated from the unresolved one: for 1<ρ<2 the paper has an exact equivalent only when B is subexponential and B_r is intermediate regularly varying.
The Weibull example should be presented as a representative heavy-tailed, subexponential, all-moments-finite case that falls outside the intermediate-regularly-varying regime.
The research target should specify that one seeks an exact asymptotic equivalent for P(D>x) as x→∞, not merely rough bounds.
refined_question: Consider the stable GI/GI/2 first-come, first-served queue with i.i.d. interarrival times τ_n of mean a, i.i.d. service times σ_n of mean b, load ρ=b/a in (1,2), and stationary waiting time D. Let B̄(x)=P{σ>x} and B̄_r(x)=b^{-1}∫_x^∞ B̄(y)dy. Determine the exact asymptotic behavior of P(D>x) as x→∞ when the service-time distribution is heavy-tailed with all power moments finite but is not in the intermediate-regularly-varying class, for example when B̄(x)=exp(-x^β) with 0<β<1.
justification: The short arXiv note 0909.0462 is an open-problems paper rather than a full theorem-proof treatment. Your draft clearly points to the specific unresolved 1<ρ<2 two-server heavy-tail case. The precise nearby context is supplied by the later Foss–Korshunov introduction: Theorem 1.2 records what is known in the GI/GI/2 case when 1<ρ<2, namely only bounds under subexponential assumptions in general, and an exact equivalent only under the stronger hypothesis that B_r is intermediate regularly varying; Theorem 1.3 explains why mentioning finiteness of all moments is relevant but not sufficient to settle the tail asymptotics; and the remark after Theorem 1.6 explicitly says that for Weibull-type B the lower and upper bounds are not of the same order and the authors do not know what the correct sharp asymptotics should be. That is why the refined question is phrased as an open exact-asymptotic problem with full model and tail notation. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/abs/0909.0462))
